statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5318(g)?
statutory.answer: No — 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting requirements are not shown to be triggered on these facts.
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5318(g) authorizes/mandates that the Secretary require a “financial institution” to report “suspicious transactions” (i.e., SAR filing) and provides related protections (e.g., confidentiality/safe harbor). To determine applicability, the facts must show (1) the actor is a covered “financial institution” subject to SAR rules, and (2) the transactions are “suspicious” under the applicable implementing regulations/thresholds, such that a SAR must be filed. Here, the entity is described as a “Securities broker / dealer firm,” which could be a covered financial institution, but the fact pattern does not state it is registered/regulated as a broker-dealer or otherwise subject to SAR obligations, nor does it describe any indicia of suspicious activity (e.g., known illicit source, structuring, fraud, sanctions nexus, unusual pattern versus expected activity). The listed wires/ACHs are large but appear broadly consistent with the declared expected monthly volume (~$48.6M) and provide no stated red flags. Therefore, whether § 5318(g) suspicious activity reporting requirements apply cannot be determined from the provided facts.
